workflow: An error-reporting routine retrieves a globally configured callback and begins invoking it.
The callback raises an exception and changes the global callback configuration during its invocation.
Failure handling releases the routine’s only strong reference to the original callback before fallback logging has finished using it.
The replacement removes the original callback’s remaining ownership, leaving fallback logging with a dangling reference.
Fallback error reporting accesses the released callback, causing a use-after-free and process termination instead of safely reporting the callback failure.
summary: Callback replacement during failure recovery causes use-after-free
